findings.title: WorkflowNavigator's 3 "NormalizedStatus" sites are actually `SliceStatus.status`, which TD-3 excludes
findings.description: The table, the component list (line 75) and step 4 of the migration plan (line 90) say to sweep 3 `=== 'complete'` sites in `WorkflowNavigator.ts`. All three are `SliceStatus` values: two `slice.status === 'complete'` comparisons, where `slice` is a `SliceStatus`, and the `status: 'complete'` return in `deriveSliceStatus()`, which returns `Promise<SliceStatus>`. TD-3 (lines 104–106) says `SliceStatus.status` is a separate lifecycle union and that rewriting it to `STATUS.Complete` would "imply the two unions are related, which they aren't." The design contradicts itself. Because `STATUS.Complete` has the literal type `'complete'`, the compiler will not catch the mistake. Fix: drop `WorkflowNavigator.ts` from the sweep, or reverse TD-3 on purpose. Recount the totals either way.

findings.title: ConsistencyChecker `detail.value` fix payloads are not classified against TD-2's vocabulary split
findings.description: About 13 of the ConsistencyChecker literals are fix payloads of the form `detail: { key: 'status', value: 'in-progress' | 'complete' }`. They describe a value to write into the `status` frontmatter field. TD-2 (line 102) says frontmatter uses a different vocabulary: `VALID_STATUSES` is `not_started`/`in_progress`/`complete`/`deferred`/`deprecated`. The design treats all 36 sites as `NormalizedStatus` comparisons ("`=== 'complete'` / `'in-progress'` comparisons across ~15 rule functions") and never decides which vocabulary these payloads belong to. If they are frontmatter-bound, sweeping them to `STATUS.*` makes `NormalizedStatus` the official source for frontmatter writes. That is the same mixing of vocabularies TD-2 calls a correctness hazard, and it would hide any existing hyphen/underscore mismatch. Fix: split ConsistencyChecker sites into comparisons and fix payloads, name the payload consumer, and state in a TD which vocabulary the payloads use.

findings.title: Literal-count success criterion is unattainable and per-file counts are inaccurate
findings.description:
The zero-match grep at line 135 excludes only `introspection/types.ts:[3-6]:`. It would still match:
- the excluded `SliceStatus` `'complete'` member in `types.ts`
- the quoted alias keys `'in-progress'` and `'not-started'` in `statusNormalizer.ts`, which line 48 says must stay literal
- the WorkflowNavigator `SliceStatus` sites
- comment text such as the `'not-started'` mention in `ProjectModelBuilder.ts` and the `// 'complete' | 'in-progress' | 'not-started'` comment in ConsistencyChecker

Several table counts also disagree with the source:
- **statusNormalizer:** 14 value-side literals plus 2 quoted keys, not "13 of 16; 3 are alias keys".
- **types.ts:** `inferredStatus` has 3 literals, not "5 of 8". The 8th match is the `SliceStatus` member.
- **ProjectModelBuilder:** its only matching literal is in a comment, not `'unknown'`.

The before/after numbers in the walkthrough (lines 150–151) depend on these counts. Fix: recount the sites, and write the success check as a per-file list of allowed lines (or one grep that excludes known allowed lines and comments) that actually returns zero matches when the sweep is done.

findings.title: Aligns with the maintenance architecture's scope and principles
findings.description: The slice matches the architecture's "Hard-coded values → configuration or constants" scope item and its "slice by theme" principle. It meets "No behavior changes without tests" by using the existing suite (with baseline counts stated) as the regression guard. Its success criteria are concrete, not open-ended.

findings.title: Exclusions and deviations from the slice plan entry are justified
findings.description: The slice plan entry names `ProjectModelBuilder.ts` as a sweep target. The design drops it with a stated reason, and the source confirms there is no live `NormalizedStatus` literal there. Leaving out the `frontmatterSchema.ts` vocabulary (TD-2), the size split of `ConsistencyChecker.ts`, and test files is reasoned and recorded under Deferred. Retyping `inferredStatus` to `NormalizedStatus` (TD-1) is a small widening change that removes a duplicate definition, and the plan correctly lands it together with the `taskFileParser.ts` sweep.

findings.title: No new I/O paths or NFR-bearing paths
findings.description: This is an internal refactor with no new I/O, message types or public API changes, and the parent architecture states no NFRs. So the slice needs no failure-mode list and no NFR targets restated.
